subject: Service diversion advisory — EU host node interruption and conditional routing instructions
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: alice@acme-retail.com, beth@neoai.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Service diversion advisory — EU host node interruption and conditional routing instructions

Hi Alice / Beth,

Quick heads up: we’re seeing an isolated failure affecting a subset of EU inferencing hosts (eu-west-1 cluster) starting ~09:05 UTC. Impact: increased errors and elevated latency for requests routed to that cluster. We’ve engaged SRE and the provider; remediation is in progress.

What we’re asking customers to do immediately (short-term mitigations):

1) Prefer regional override (recommended) — instruct your clients to prefer a different region while we remediate. You can set the region hint header or query param. Example:

curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=us-west-2"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"prompt":"Hello","max_tokens":128}'

Or set the header: "X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2" if your client supports it.

2) Enable conditional sidecar/fallback (if you use our SDK) — set fallback_region="us-west-2" in the client config. This will automatically route to a healthy cluster for requests that would otherwise hit the affected EU node.

3) Short-term model variant: if you rely on a specific large-LLM hosted in EU, consider switching to the compatible quantized variant in the US pool (model: rw-13b-q) to avoid rate-limited regional queues.

We’ll keep the status page updated here: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/EU-2026-07-20. I’ve attached a one-page action checklist (customer-action-checklist.csv) and our internal traffic-split guidance (incident-20260720-traffic-split.pdf) for your ops team.

Next steps from our side:
- SRE (Marcus/Jonas) are validating node-level health and starting a targeted restart.
- We’ll provide a post-incident timeline and RCA within 48 hours.

If you want us to manage the cutover for you (we can toggle region-level routing on your account temporarily), reply with a preferred fallback region (us-west-2 or us-east-1) and a contact number for a short 15-minute window.

Apologies for the interruption — we’re treating this as a priority.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Lead, North America
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0182

--

Alice — thanks, we’ve enabled account-level temporary fallback to us-west-2 for Acme Retail as requested. Summary of the config change we applied:

- Routing: account override = us-west-2 (effective immediately)
- TTL: 12 hours (will auto-revert unless you request extension)
- Cache behavior: session prefix caching is preserved via our cross-region KV replication for prefixes less than 2kB; however, very recent KV writes (<30s) to the affected EU nodes may not have replicated before the outage. Please treat any in-flight writes around 09:00–09:10 UTC as potentially partial — we will surface per-request error codes if we detect missing KV entries.

We confirmed the following with SRE:
- Root cause likely a networking flapping event on the hypervisor fabric affecting a subset of EU hosts.
- We’ve drained affected hosts and are running validation checks; a rolling restart is underway.

Call details: 10:00 UTC Zoom — joining details shared in separate calendar invite. Evelyn will be on the call to capture action items and own the postmortem packaging.

If you notice errors after the failover, please send a single representative request id and sample payload so we can trace immediately.

Laura

Subject: EU cluster incident update and next steps (post-incident summary)

Hi all,

Post-incident summary (brief):
- Incident window: 2026-07-20 09:05–2026-07-20 11:40 UTC
- Impact: intermittent 5xx and elevated p95 latency for ~18% of EU routed traffic; Acme Retail saw 502 spikes between 09:10–09:25 UTC.
- Immediate mitigations: account fallback to us-west-2 applied at 09:50 UTC; cross-region routing preserved prefix cache for most sessions.

Root cause (preliminary): transient networking flap in third-party cloud hypervisor that caused control-plane routing inconsistency for a subset of EU hosts. Affected hosts showed packet loss and TCP resets; we drained and restarted the hosts, and provider confirmed fabric stabilization at ~11:20 UTC. We marked the cluster healthy after validation and rebalanced load; final checks finished at 11:40 UTC.

Customer impact notes:
- Short-lived cache inconsistencies could affect very recent KV writes; we recommend validating any critical session state that was being updated near the window. We will surface a filtered list of request ids where KV write failures were detected (separate secure link).
- No data exfiltration or long-term data loss identified.

Follow-up actions and timeline:
- Within 48 hours: full RCA doc and timeline (INF-4721) — link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4721
- 72 hours: provider action confirmation and any change to regional capacity allocation.
- Ops recommendation: if you need stronger cross-region affinity for session-critical apps, we can schedule a configuration change to enable synchronous KV replication to the topologically closest healthy region (note: additional cost and small latency tradeoff).

Attachments: incident-20260720-traffic-split.pdf (internal engineer guidance), customer-action-checklist.csv (actions we ran on your account).

If you’d like us to keep the account-level fallback in place longer while you validate session data, reply with the desired TTL (12h / 24h / 72h) and we’ll apply it.

Thanks again for the quick coordination. Evelyn will share the formal RCA and the list of affected request ids via a secure link within 48 hours.

Best,
